meta.name: Atelier Craft
meta.notes: Linen/kraft palette stays fixed; primary inks the rotating stamp, script accents, handwritten prices, buttons, marquee ribbon and the perforated postage-stamp CTA (text-ink uses are mixed 72% with dark text so pastels stay readable); accent tints the washi tape and footer link hovers.

issues: Catastrophic: every .rv element and every price tag was set to opacity:0 until an IntersectionObserver fired. In the full-page renders more than half of the homepage is blank parchment: no story, stats, gallery, quote, postage CTA or footer on desktop; on mobile the whole product wall is just empty twine lines; on the Birth Bear stress test even the process timeline and its heading are missing.
Catalog: the postage-stamp CTA is invisible, leaving roughly 1,300px of dead space between the last row of tags and the footer.
Catalog stamp badge: 'producten' breaks mid-word ('producte / n') because of overflow-wrap:anywhere, so the signature badge looks broken.
Stress hero: the script accent plus its swash underline is wider than the copy column and runs into the deckled photo.
Home rhythm: the process ruler and the shop heading are separated by about 300px of double section padding, so the page sags in the middle.
Hiding content by default is fragile. If JS lags or the page is captured without scrolling, the signature hanging tags never show at all.
fixed: Replaced the hide-until-scrolled reveal with a progressive enhancement: content is always rendered, and sections entering the viewport get a short stamped 'settle' (translate + slight rotate). Tags still play their swing-on-the-twine drop. This brings back the story, stats, polaroid gallery, quote, postage CTA, footer, the mobile product wall and the stress-test timeline (template.html + catalog.html).
Catalog CTA and footer render again, so the empty gap is gone.
Catalog stamp: the count now never breaks mid-word. The number sits large on the first line, the label small underneath, and the centre is tilted -8deg like a hand-pressed stamp.
Hero script accent is capped to the copy column (max-width minus its indent), so long accents and their swash no longer cross into the photo.
Tightened the space between the process section and the shop so the ruler leads straight into the twine of price tags.
